paragraphs.source_en:
agent of darkness. Cp. S.’s accusation of the government prosecutors of the bookseller Richard Carlile
on a charge of blasphemy, for whom religion ‘is the mask & the garment by which they are invested
with the symbols of worldly power’ (L ii 143). In 1815 Sidmouth and Lord Liverpool planned to intro-
duce a bill in Parliament to provide new churches for the increasing population in industrial areas,
which was withdrawn for lack of funds; though in 1818, Sidmouth supported a similar and this time
successful bill to raise £1,000,000 for the purpose. See note to ll. 238–41 and 240–41.
